text.p: Here are highlights of stories in Romania's press on Wednesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy:
Business:
ADEVARUL

- Troubled commercial banks Banca Dacia Felix SA and Renasterea Creditului Romanesc SA should officially announce their inability to meet depositors' demands to redeem their money. Depositors are to be compensated by the central bank.
TINERETUL LIBER
- The association of Romanian businessmen will launch a programme to finance investment projects in the private sector.
- The Swedish concern ABB officially opened an electrical engineering factory in Romania. Investment in the project amounts to $5.0 million.
- The central bank is launching a new, 50,000-leu banknote on Wednesday.
AZI
- The Zephir consorium, grouping Motorola of the United States, Tele Denmark and Norway's Telnor, are contesting the results of the tender for a GSM licence in Romania.
- Romania's government approved the export of 500,000 tonnes of wheat this year.
ZIUA
- Prices of several stocks traded on the over-the-counter market fell below 100 lei under heavy supply.
- The 1997 state budget drafted by the outgoing government put next year's inflation rate at an estimated 25 percent.
CRONICA ROMANA

- The dismantling of the National Oil Company does not mean Romania will not be able to import crude oil this winter, Petrogaz SA president Teodor Vostinaru says in an interview. The government guarantees external credits for oil imports and it will decide who is to make those imports, he added.
CURIERUL NATIONAL
- A new company, Electroceramica SA, joins in trading on the stock exchange starting Thursday.
General:
All the newspaper report the designation of Bucharest mayor Victor Ciorbea as Prime Minister.
ROMANIA LIBERA

- The newspaper publishes the final results of the November 17 presidential run-off and the distribution of the votes given to reformist academic Emil Constantinescu who defeated incumbent Ion Iliescu.

- The ethnic Hungarians' vote denounced intolerance and political diversions, said Gyorgy Frunda, member of the Hungarian Democratic Union (UDMR). The 1.6 million Hungarians in Romania voted for Constantinescu, against Iliescu.
- Adrian Nastase, executive president of the leftist Party of Social Democracy (PDSR), said his party might leave parliament if Iliescu's mandate as senator is not validated.
EVENIMENTUL ZILEI
- The newspaper publishes a report on the CIA agent Harold Nicholson, arrested over alleged espionage for Russia.
ADEVARUL
- The newspaper publishes the message from Romania's ex-King Michael congratulating the Romanian people on the election outcome.
- Russian President Boris Yeltsin and the United States saluted the election of Emil Constantinescu.
CRONICA ROMANA
- Victor Babiuc, justice minister in the first post-communist cabinet led by Prime Minister Petre Roman is likely to be appointed Defence Minister.
AZI
- Hungarian Foreign Minister Laszlo Kovacs said Romanian-Hungarian relations would be broadened. He said Constantinescu's victory was encouraging.
CURIERUL NATIONAL
- General Dumitru Cioflina, Romanian army chief of staff, says in an interview that reform in the army would be completed by the year 2000.
ZIUA

- The National Peasant Party (PNT-CD), major party in the CDR bloc, is governing again after 63 years, reads a front-page headline on the appointment of PNT-CD member Victor Ciorbea as Prime Minister.

- Ioan Mihai Pacepa, head of the Securitate secret police under Communist dictator Nicolae Ceausescu until 1977, when he defected to the United States, congratulates Constantinescu and promises support to "eradicate the Kremlin legacy in Romania."
- The United States is offering $350 million in aid to improve sanitation conditions in Bucharest's schools. ($=3,500 lei) -- Bucharest Newsroom 40-1 3120264
